title: Common persistent-node normalization atlas
statement: Let $R,K$ be commutative rings and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A common persistent normalization chart consists of a commutative ring $A$, a coefficient morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, a standard model $M$ [def-trf-strict-semistable-curve], an affine scheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}P$, and etale maps $p:U\to X$ and $q:U\to M$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] commuting with the maps to $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The coefficient and model are either (i) $A$ is a DVR [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $b$ is etale, and $M=\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv))$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-\varpi^n))$ for a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $n\geq0$, or (ii) $A$ is a field with a finite etale map $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $g\eta=b$, and $M=\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv))$ or $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$. In the intended use $K$ is a field and the finite etale map is precisely a finite separable field extension. On a split model, the pullback of the componentwise normalization $X^\nu\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] to $U$ is isomorphic over $U$ to the pullback [def-pc-fibre-product] of $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u]\times A[v])\to\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv))$, induced by $u\mapsto(u,0)$ and $v\mapsto(0,v)$; on every other model the pulled-back normalization is an isomorphism. A common persistent normalization atlas chooses such a chart above every point $x\in X$, whose map to $X$ has $x$ in its image. No global ordering of branches is included. The canonical origin map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to M$ sends both coordinates to zero, and the canonical two-origin map $\operatorname{Spec}(A\times A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is induced by the diagonal ring homomorphism. These maps use the polynomial rings of [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The origin ideal sheaf on the split model is the ideal generated by the quotient coordinates $u,v$, transported to global sections by the canonical spectrum-sections isomorphism.
